Ninety-two days, one hundred and forty-two trades, a steady climb interrupted by a single ugly week in late March — and yet the quarter closes near its high. Most of the damage came from sticking around past one in the morning, when prices were drifting and you were stubborn.

Cumulative R since the opening week of the quarter. The hatched region marks an eight-day drawdown of −8.4R in late March — the worst stretch of the year — triggered by three losing London opens and one over-leveraged Sweep & Flip on XAUUSD.

02—Where you make money
A small heatmap with one obvious truth: this is a London-session book, whether you admit it or not.
“

Your London sessions returned +28.3R this quarter — more than Asian and New‑York combined.

— Filed under Session study · 02·iii

The London window (07:00–11:00 UTC) carried 59% of all closed P&L. Asian (00:00–07:00) ran net flat. The New-York open underperformed despite a comparable trade count — your average loss there is −0.94R, against −0.61R in London. The discipline gap is visible; it is also expensive.

Marginalia

The quarter's best day was April 20th, when three Continuation Type A entries on EURUSD compounded into a clean +6.4R. You stopped trading at 11:40 UTC — a rare and well-judged exit.

The worst day was March 23rd, the trough of the eight-day drawdown — a single counter-trend short on XAUUSD ran −3.8R before you closed it manually, well past your written stop.

You broke even on twelve days this quarter. Half of them clustered around economic-calendar releases. Worth treating as a feature, not a defect.
